*Alico Closes Fiscal Year 2026 with $34.1 million of Land Sales and Approximately* *91% of Total Acres Being Leased*


*Net Income Attributable to Alico, Inc. Common Stockholders of $6.6 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $22.1 million for Fiscal Year 2026, Exceeding Guidance of Approximately $15.0 Million*


*Cash and Cash Equivalents of $52.6 million as of September 30, 2026, Extending Cash Runway Through Fiscal Year 2029 Without Requiring Additional Asset Sales*


*Corkscrew Grove Villages Continues to Progress Through State and Federal Permitting Following Local Entitlement Approval*


FORT MYERS, Fla., Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Alico, Inc. (“Alico” or the “Company,” “we,” “us” or “our”) (Nasdaq: ALCO) today announced financial results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended September 30, 2026.


**Management Comment**


John Kiernan, President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, stated, “Fiscal year 2026 was a year of steady progress with our diversified land strategy.


"With our citrus operation wind-down largely behind us, our attention during fiscal year 2026 turned towards optimizing our land portfolio for our shareholders. We realized more than $34.0 million in opportunistic land sales, which also exceeded management's estimates for value. We invested approximately $2.0 million through the acquisition of the portion of Citree that we didn't own to continue to consolidate our ownership of acres within our 20,000 acre Joshua Grove in Arcadia. Our land leasing program to other operators has been rigorous, and now approximately 91% of our total acres are leased for productive use."


"Net Income attributable to Alico was $6.6 million for fiscal year 2026 and Adjusted EBITDA was $22.1 million, significantly exceeding our previously announced guidance of approximately $15 million. We ended the year with cash and cash equivalents of $52.6 million, ahead of our guidance of approximately $48 million, net debt of $32.7 million and approximately $92.5 million of available borrowing capacity. We believe that our cash balance creates a competitive liquidity advantage for Alico and that this cash balance will allow us to fund our operations through fiscal year 2029 without requiring additional asset sales and to advance our development pipeline on our own timeline.”


“Looking ahead, our mission does not change. We intend to continue to opportunistically sell non-strategic assets. We will build strong relationships with agricultural lessees as appropriate. We intend to seek to maximize lease income on our agricultural acreage for the long-term. We will continue to prioritize entitlement-driven work on our highest value properties with management attention, financial resources, and capital when necessary. Our Corkscrew Grove East Village project continues to progress through state and federal permitting channels following its local entitlement approval in April 2026. We continue to expect important approval milestones in 2027.


“In addition to liquidity, we believe that consistency in our strategy is a competitive advantage and serves our shareholders well. Combined with our long-standing commitment to responsible land stewardship and conservation as part of our agricultural roots, we believe that the entitlement progress, land leasing and selected sales that we demonstrated in 2026 will continue to position us to realize the value that we see in our approximately 47,200-acre portfolio.”

For the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported net income attributable to Alico common stockholders of $6.6 million, compared to a net loss attributable to Alico common stockholders of $147.3 million for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025. The net income for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026 was driven by gains on the sale of property and equipment of $25.1 million and approximately $6.6 million of contingent lease payments received from a lessee for crop insurance payments because of weather events. The net loss for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, is principally attributable to accelerated depreciation of $162.7 million, the impairment of our young trees and the impairment of certain long lived assets at one of our groves, of $25.0 million, as a result of our Strategic Transformation, partially offset by gains on the sale of property and equipment of $21.8 million and $20.4 million of crop insurance proceeds received during the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, in connection with Hurricane Milton, as well as an income tax benefit of $38.4 million. For the fiscal year ended September 30, 2026, the Company had earnings of $0.88 per diluted common share, compared to a loss of $19.29 per diluted common share for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025.


When both periods are adjusted for certain items, including the impairment of long-lived assets and restructuring and other charges, the Company had an Adjusted EBITDA for the fiscal years ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 of $22.1 million and $22.5 million, respectively.


Historically, the Company was primarily engaged in citrus production and sales, which created significant seasonal patterns, with the first and second quarters typically generating most annual revenue. As part of the Strategic Transformation, the Company has substantially completed the wind down of its citrus operations, having completed its last significant citrus harvest in April 2025, and now focuses on land sales, land leasing and land development activities. The Company expects the historical seasonal patterns to diminish now that the transition is substantially complete, and, because land sales and development milestones may be recognized on different timing, results for any quarter may not be indicative of results for the full year.


**Other Corporate Financial Information**


General and administrative expenses increased $0.4 million for the year ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the year ended September 30, 2025, due to an increase in employee costs, including stock-based compensation, contract labor costs and a provision for credit losses on certain citrus receivables, partially offset by lower depreciation expense.


Other expense, net, for the years ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 decreased $2.0 million as a result of the increase in interest income due to higher average cash on hand and a decrease in interest expense due to lower borrowings under our lines of credit during the year ended September 30, 2026.


**Dividend**


On October 16, 2026, the Company paid a fourth quarter cash dividend of $0.05 per share on its outstanding common stock to stockholders of record as of October 2, 2026.


**Balance Sheet and Liquidity**


The Company continues to demonstrate financial strength within its balance sheet, as highlighted below:


- Cash and cash equivalents were $52.6 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $14.5 million from September 30, 2025.
- Total debt was $85.4 million and net debt was $32.7 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $85.5 million and $47.4 million, respectively, at September 30, 2025.
- The Company’s working capital was $46.9 million at September 30, 2026, representing a 7.04 to 1.00 current ratio.
- The Company maintains a solid debt to total assets ratio. At September 30, 2026 and 2025, the ratios were 0.44 to 1.00 and 0.43 to 1.00, respectively.
- Available borrowings under our line of credit were $92.5 million, at September 30, 2026.


**Land Sales, Leasing and Capital Allocation**


During fiscal year 2026, the Company completed land sales of $34.1 million, including the January 2026 sale of approximately 2,950 acres for $26.9 million, which generated a gain of approximately $19.8 million. The Company owns approximately 47,200 acres across 7 Florida counties.


The Company’s diversified land management programs, including agricultural leases, sod, and rock and sand royalty arrangements, continued to perform during the year, and approximately 91% of the Company’s acreage was leased as of September 30, 2026. In the third quarter, the Company entered into an agricultural lease agreement for approximately 3,280 acres in Hendry County, structured with an option to purchase the property for $29.5 million, or $9,000 per acre, a price that holds through June 2029 and escalates annually thereafter.


During fiscal year 2026, the Company also repurchased 245,399 shares for approximately $10.0 million under its $50 million share repurchase program and declared regular quarterly cash dividends totaling $0.20 per share.


**Real Estate and Land Development**


In June 2025, the Florida Legislature established the Corkscrew Grove Stewardship District. Stewardship districts are independent special districts authorized to plan, finance, construct, operate and maintain public infrastructure in planned developments, operating on the principle that growth pays for itself. Similar districts are used in communities like Ave Maria and Lakewood Ranch.


In March 2025, the Company announced the creation of Corkscrew Grove Villages located on approximately 4,600 acres at the northwest corner of Collier County on the border of Lee and Hendry counties. These two master planned developments are expected to comply with the County’s 1,500- acre cap for Villages, and be accompanied by approximately 7,000 acres of permanent conservation areas. The plan for both villages is to feature approximately 9,000 homes, including approximately 750 affordable housing units total for essential workers, and approximately 480,000 square feet of commercial space offering retail, dining, office, and medical uses. The East Village includes an additional 100,000 square feet for indoor self-storage and a minimum of 45,020 square feet of civic uses, and the West Village may include similar additional uses depending on County requirements and future site planning.


Alico launched its multi-year entitlement process for Corkscrew Grove Villages by submitting an application to Collier County for local approval for the first of the two villages, the East Village. The Company has also submitted permit applications to the South Florida Water Management District and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers for both villages.


In April 2026, Alico received final local entitlement approvals from the Collier County Board of County Commissioners for the East Village component of Corkscrew Grove Villages. The approved East Village Stewardship Receiving Area (SRA) covers approximately 1,446.59 acres and provides for up to 4,502 dwelling units, including 362 affordable housing units, and up to 238,606 square feet of retail and office uses. This advances the project toward obtaining the required federal permits from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, as well as the state permits from the South Florida Water Management District. Construction on the first village could begin in 2028 or 2029 if all approvals are granted.


In June 2026, Alico acquired the remaining 49% ownership interest in Citree, a joint venture through which the Company held a 51% interest in approximately 1,200 acres of land in DeSoto County, for $2.0 million in cash, plus potential contingent consideration and the assumption of all of Citree’s approximately $3.3 million of outstanding debt. Following the transaction, Alico owns 100% of the entity and its underlying acreage. The Company believes this transaction simplifies its corporate structure and gives it full ownership and control over the future use of this property, consistent with its broader strategy of streamlining the business.


Alico maintains a strong commitment to regional conservation, having transferred lands over the past 40 years that became part of the Corkscrew Regional Ecosystem Watershed (CREW), Tiger Creek Preserve and Okaloacoochee Slough Wildlife Management Area. In 2023, Alico sold more than 17,000 acres of land from central Hendry County, commonly referred to as Devil’s Garden, to the Florida Department of Environmental Protection as part of the Florida Forever program. Since Devil’s Garden was added to the Florida Forever Priority List in 2002, Alico has sold or entered easements to protect more than 46,800 acres within the project boundaries. Combined with approximately 7,000 acres expected to be placed in conservation as part of the Corkscrew Grove Villages proposal, these efforts support the implementation of the Florida Wildlife Corridor.


The plan for Corkscrew Grove Villages aligns with the Collier Rural Land Stewardship Area (RLSA) program, an innovative, incentive-based approach to sustainable rural growth that has received national recognition. The villages will enhance public infrastructure and provide significant economic benefit to the region at no additional cost to taxpayers.

**About Alico**


Alico, Inc. (Nasdaq: ALCO) is a Florida-based agribusiness and land management company with over 125 years of experience. Following its strategic transformation in 2025, Alico operates as a diversified land company with approximately 47,200 acres across 7 Florida counties as of September 30, 2026. The Company focuses on strategic land development opportunities and diversified agricultural operations, leveraging its extensive land portfolio to create long-term shareholder value while maintaining its commitment to responsible land stewardship and conservation. Learn more about Alico at www.alicoinc.com.

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


In addition to the measurements prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (“U.S. GAAP”), Alico utilizes EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Net Debt, which are non-GAAP financial measures within the meaning of Regulation G and Item 10(e) of Regulation S-K, to evaluate the performance of its business in the case of EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA, and liquidity, in the case of Net Debt. As we advance our long-term diversified land and real estate strategy, we believe Adjusted EBITDA provides a clear view of our core operating results.


Due to significant depreciable assets associated with the nature of our operations and, to a lesser extent, interest costs associated with our capital structure, management believes that EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA and Net Debt are important measures to evaluate our results of operations between periods on a more comparable basis and to help investors analyze underlying trends in our business, evaluate the performance, in the case of EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, and liquidity, in the case of Net Debt, of our business both on an absolute basis and relative to our peers and the broader market, provide useful information to both management and investors by excluding certain non-cash and other items that may not be indicative of our core operating results and operational strength of our business and help investors evaluate our ability to service our debt. Such measurements are not prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP and should not be construed as an alternative to reported results determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The non-GAAP information provided is unique to Alico and may not be consistent with methodologies used by other companies. EBITDA is defined as net income (loss) attributable to Alico, Inc. common stockholders before interest expense, net, income tax benefit (provision), and depreciation, depletion and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as EBITDA as further adjusted for impairment of long-lived assets and restructuring and other charges. Net Debt is defined as Current portion of long-term debt, Long-term debt, net and Lines of credit, less cash.
